entries.name: Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing Site

facts.claim: DOC lists Puhi Kai Iti/Cooks Landing National Historic Reserve under Gisborne area, where the first European set foot on New Zealand soil.
Cook Monument unveiled 1906; Cook's crew sighted NZ on 7 Oct 1769 and landed two days later; reserve upgraded 2019 and renamed Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing National Historic Reserve.
OSM relation 'Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing National Historic Reserve' centre -38.67545,178.02525 and 'Cook Monument' node -38.67534,178.02549.

entries.ticketUrl_note: Verified: loads (200), title 'Gisborne area: Places to go in the East Coast region'; body names Puhi Kai Iti/Cooks Landing National Historic Reserve. DOC is the managing agency; no separate reserve page found, so the area page is the link. Hours (always open) not stated by a source: open public reserve, treat as approximate.
unverified: 24-hour access

entries.name: Eastwoodhill Arboretum

facts.claim: Open 9am-4pm, 7 days a week, closed Christmas Day; at 2392 Wharekopae Rd, Ngatapa.
Entry: adults $18, senior (65+) $15, child 5-16 $5, under 5 free, family $45; after-hours access not allowed.
Over 25,000 species of trees, shrubs and climbers; 25 km of trails and tracks including a steep climb up Mt Arateitei; National Arboretum of NZ.
Wikivoyage: 35 km north-west of Gisborne, New Zealand's largest planting of North American trees, lovely in autumn.

unverified: visit time (2-4 h is an estimate; site offers 25 km of tracks)

entries.name: Rere Rock Slide

facts.claim: Natural 60 m rock slide at about 30 degrees on the Wharekopae River, slid on boogie boards or tyres; in the AA's 101 Must-do places for Kiwis.
Tourism board: 'one of our fantastic free activities and open all-year round', free parking on site, within 46 km of Gisborne, address Wharekopae Road.
Rere Falls (5 m high, 20 m wide, can walk behind) are just around the bend on the same river; Rere Reserve has picnic area and toilets.
OSM node 'Rere Falls & Rockslides' at -38.53908,177.59066; separate 'Rere Falls' node -38.53736,177.60958.

entries.name: Mōrere Springs Scenic Reserve

facts.claim: Nga Hua o Mōrere hot springs at the main entrance to the scenic reserve; hours Thursday-Monday 10am-5pm, closed Tuesday and Wednesday (DOC page; DOC also says check Facebook for updates).
Prices: adult $20, child (5-18) $12, kaumatua/senior $14; family first adult and child full price then 50%.
Reserve is on SH2, 40 km north-east of Wairoa, 52 km south of Gisborne and 15 km north of Nuhaka; 364 ha of rainforest with nikau palms, walks.
Natural salt-water hot springs producing 250,000 L a day, piped to pools in native forest.

OSM: 'Morere Hot Springs' attraction node at -38.98668,177.79202; 'Morere Pool' way centre -38.98642,177.79158; placement point -38.98271,177.80592 is the centre of the Scenic Reserve relation (18235552), ~1.3 km east of the springs.

entries.name: Young Nick's Head

facts.claim: A Gisborne tourism guide says public access to the headland is restricted/private land (private farmland), best treated as a viewpoint seen from Kaiti Hill, Kaiti Beach, Wainui Beach and the waterfront.

Wikipedia: after 2002 protests the cliffs, summit and archaeological sites were gifted into public ownership as a National Historic Reserve, the rest of the station under covenants; now Te Kuri a Paoa/Young Nick's Head National Historic Reserve. It was the first land sighted by Cook's crew on 6 Oct 1769. Article does not mention a monument, walking track or car park.

entries.name: Anaura Bay

facts.claim: DOC: camp on a beautiful beach or walk to panoramic views on the nearby track; turn off SH35 onto Anaura Road about 67 km north of Gisborne, campsite a further 8.7 km.
Cook entered the bay on 21 October 1769 and Endeavour filled casks from Hawai Stream where a plaque records it.
Wikipedia: Cook landed at the southern end where a village and motor camp now are; a scenic reserve at the northern end has a walkway and campsite; named one of NZ's best beaches.
OSM: Anaura Bay Motor Camp (way) -38.24751,178.31661; Anaura Bay Campsite (DOC conservation campsite) -38.23336,178.30822.

entries.name: Lake Waikaremoana Great Walk

facts.claim: 46 km one way, 3-4 days, intermediate tramping track; walked from Onepoto in the south or Hopuruahine in the north, not a circuit.

No fees to enter Te Urewera or walk a day walk on the track; per person per night: huts adult $35 (child 5-17 $18), campsites adult $19 (child $9); huts and campsites must be booked ahead; bookings open for 2026/27.
Hopuruahine Landing is the northern track end; Onepoto Shelter is the southern start. DOC lists a trail-end car park at Onepoto.
OSM place node 'Hopuruahine Landing' -38.71694,177.05176; Onepoto Road centre -38.80114,177.12226 (road to the start); the exact Onepoto shelter/car-park point was not found.
Wikipedia gives 44 km and season 'summer to autumn'; DOC gives 46 km.

entries.name: Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park

facts.claim: Park is 90 km south-east of Rotorua off Te Whaiti Rd via SH38; the most popular entrance is past Minginui village and up River Road to the River Road car park, the start of many walks.

Located in the Bay of Plenty and East Coast regions; tracks, huts and campsites (overnight huts need passes); river levels rise fast in heavy rain, regular track washouts April-August; stinging nettle present.

entries.name: Māhia Peninsula

facts.claim: Māhia Beach is a safe, shallow family beach good for paddle boarding and surfing, parking along the road, public toilets next to the beach by the Māhia Fishing and Boating Club; reached by SH2 to Nuhaka then straight on to Māhia.

Māhia Peninsula Scenic Reserve: 374 ha, one of the last tracts of lowland coastal forest on the East Coast; 3.5 km loop (~2.5 h), trig Te Kapu 397 m, dogs/camping prohibited, 7 km south of Māhia Beach along Kinikini Road.
Wikipedia: Māhia is known for surf, scuba diving, hiking and fishing; Mōrere Hot Springs 15 minutes away.

Wikipedia: the wharf (about 600 m) is the second longest in NZ after Tiwai Point (1,500 m); built 1920s, restored and re-opened 2013.

entries.name: Te Urewera (destination name and description check)

facts.claim: Te Urewera National Park was disestablished in 2014 and replaced by 'Te Urewera', a legal entity with legal personhood, governed by the Te Urewera Board (Tūhoe and Crown); the Wikipedia article title is 'Te Urewera'.

DOC: Te Urewera is recognised in NZ law as a living person, governed by a board; care of tracks and facilities by Te Uru Taumatua (Ngāi Tūhoe); huts are being removed; SH38 is gravel for about 90 km between Murupara and Tuai.
